steps.text: To Marinate: In a large nonporous glass dish or bowl, combine the sour cream, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, celery salt, paprika, salt, pepper and garlic; mix well. Add chicken breasts and coat well with sour cream marinade. Cover dish or bowl and refrigerate to marinate for at least 8 hours, or overnight.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Place bread crumbs in a shallow dish or bowl. Remove chicken from marinade and discard marinade. Dredge chicken in bread crumbs to coat well and place in 2 lightly greased 9x13 inch baking dishes. In a small saucepan or skillet, melt butter and spoon evenly over chicken.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 60 to 70 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and fork-tender and juices run clear.

raw_recipe.headline: Sour Cream Marinated Chicken II
raw_recipe.description: Bone-in chicken breasts marinated in a seasoned sour cream mixture, then breaded and baked. This recipe is surprisingly easy and tasty for people of all ages.

review.reviewBody: I used a slight altered version of this recipe...did not use the celery salt or black pepper and used Pepperidge Farm herb seasoned breadcrumbs. This was awesome and all of my three children had third helpings of this chicken. I will be making this on a regular basis.

I was surprised at how good it was. However I made changes. I used boneless chicken breasts cut in half and then pounded down until it’s a cutlet I added 1 cup of Hellmans light mayonnaise to one cup sour cream and added chicken to baggie with marinade for a few hours. I used Pepperidge Farm herb stuffing rolled out to crumbs. My husband who doesn’t like chicken loved it. Butter on top before baking was key.
I doubled this with no problem. Ended up not having any breadcrumbs so I used pulverized pretzels. Delicious.

I use this strictly as the title implies, as a marinade. Then I coat in seasoned flour and fry, generally I use boneless skinless chicken as it cooks super quick and this marinade adds To the flavor in the moistness

I seasoned boneless chicken breasts w/ a little bit of celery salt, garlic powder, black pepper & parsley flakes. I cooked the chicken in the slow cooker about 4 hrs. on high & about 1 hr. on low. Afterward, I poured the sour cream marinade over the chicken & set the slow cooker to the serve setting. I did not bread & bake it afterward. You must like sour cream to enjoy this recipe.
Much better if bread crumbs are replaced with corn flake crumbs.......makes all the difference
Much better if bread crumbs are replaced with corn flake crumbs.......makes all the difference

Moist, flavorful, crispy on both sides. It's a keeper! I did decide to use panko on half of the breasts & on the other breasts I used bread crumbs with some dry Italian seasoning. Both versions were excellent.

I made a few minor modifications to the recipe. First, I used fat free sour cream in the marinade. I left out the butter completely, instead I sprayed the chicken with cooking spray so it would get crunchy. This tasted really good. The chicken was very moist and flavorful. This recipe will stay in my recipe box.

A++ I used boneless, skinless chicken breasts, and substituted a little creole seasoning (that we ALL love here in south Louisiana) for the salt, pepper, and celery salt. I served it for company and they loved it! A definite keeper!

Delicious! My husband and I loved it. I used boneless, skinless chicken breast halves and substituted season salt for the celery salt (I didn't have any on hand). Unlike another reviewer, I really think that spooning the melted butter over top should NOT be skipped. It made the breading soft and delicious. I recommend this recipe.

I marinated longer than the recipe said, approximately 24 hours. This recipe wasn't bad by any means, but that being said, did not stand out in any way to me. I found it lacking in flavor and excitement. I feel like I've had 100 breaded chicken recipes that taste just like this. A bit disappointed.
It is moist chicken, but the flavor of the marinade isn't present. Left the chicken in the marinade for 40+ hours.
Absolutely delicious.

Okay but I had no bread crumbs so I used panko. I also left itin oven too long so it was slightly burnt and very dry. All my fault. Might try it again using bread crumbs and WILL pay attention to time.
Great recipe. To all those who modify the recipe the give it a low rating, shame on you. Rate on the originality and not on your own failure.
It's just lovely,,, it's easy to make, simple and result is stunning... Thank you for the recipe..
Made this for dinner tonight- fantastic! Def will make again.
I have made this recipe with chicken breasts instead of bone-in for the last 15-20 years. Serve it with tri veggies with toasted almonds and chicken Rice a Roni. It is awesome!!

I was a little leery of the ingredients, but they turned out great! I didn't have any bone-in breasts so I used it for boneless breasts - this was the only change I made (I feel you shouldn't review a recipe unless you prepare it the way it was written). My family loved it! It was quite moist and very tasty.
